questions.q: What does a REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING error indicate?
options: A field marked required on the object was left blank in the import file
A lookup field pointed at a record that doesn't exist
A validation rule blocked the save
A Unique field already has that value elsewhere
questions.explain: This error fires when a required field has no value supplied for that row.

questions.q: Why is DUPLICATE_VALUE easy to confuse with the Duplicate Rules from earlier in the course?
options: They are actually the same mechanism, just named differently
DUPLICATE_VALUE only appears when a Duplicate Rule is deactivated
Both involve the word 'duplicate,' but DUPLICATE_VALUE is a hard Unique-field constraint, unrelated to Duplicate Rules
DUPLICATE_VALUE always means a Duplicate Rule needs to be created
questions.explain: DUPLICATE_VALUE comes from a field-level Unique constraint and fires on every insert regardless of Duplicate Rule configuration. The actual Duplicate Rule equivalent is DUPLICATE_DETECTED.

questions.q: What does the rest of a FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION error message contain?
options: A generic Salesforce system message with no further detail
A list of every validation rule on the object
The Salesforce Id of the record that failed
The specific Error Message text configured on the validation rule that blocked the save
questions.explain: This error includes the validation rule's own configured Error Message, telling you exactly what needs to be fixed on that row.

questions.q: 150 rows fail with INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY, all referencing the same missing AccountId. What's the most efficient next step?
options: Manually edit and re-import each of the 150 rows one at a time
Fix or load the single missing Account, then re-import just those 150 rows
Delete the AccountId column from the file entirely
Re-import the entire original file, including rows that already succeeded
questions.explain: Sorting the error file reveals one dominant root cause. Fixing that single Account and re-importing only the previously-failed rows clears most or all of the file efficiently.

questions.q: Why should you re-import only the previously-failed rows rather than the entire original file?
options: Re-running already-successful rows risks unwanted duplicates or unnecessary re-matching
Data Loader technically cannot process a file containing any previously-successful rows
The full file is always too large for a single batch
Error files cannot be combined with success files under any circumstance
questions.explain: Rows that already succeeded don't need to run again — doing so risks creating duplicates on insert operations or unnecessary updates, and wastes time re-processing what already worked.
